title: Not a Fool
reviewNotes: All 18 saved states and narration reviewed; native image 16 establishes the complete seven-piece final fork after Kb7 at 52s. White Kh1/Nc8/g2/h3 versus Black Kb7/Qe7/Bg3. Source Nxe7 wins exactly; independent Nd6+/Qxd6 loses. Two branches, four distinct tablebase positions, three encoded moves. Earlier rook/queen offers and capture-underpromotion belong to the larger source context, not the exact checked root.
transcript: White is not a fool. It might seem like black is up a bishop, but white has a secret resource in this position starting with rook to c8 check. Now, of course, if the king takes, we simply take a rook for free. So, black takes the rook, and if we now promote to a queen, after the king captures, black simply has an extra piece and white loses, which is why the only winning move for white in this position is the stunning queen takes a salmon check. Not capturing back the rook and giving away another entire queen to the black pieces. And despite white only having three pawns left and black being up 14 points of material, white is completely winning thanks to the incredible underpromotion to a knight that forks the king and queen. Now, after the king moves, the white knight captures the queen, and having the two extra pawns, white is going to win this game.
